item.content:encoded:
A little late to the party, but:

“ … [D]anger does not really affect an SCP's Object Class. As has been reiterated several times above this, an item's Object Class is more based on the difficulty of containment rather than the danger it otherwise poses. For example, a button that can destroy the entire universe when it's pressed would be safe, whereas a cat who randomly switches places with another cat anywhere on earth would be considered Keter. ”

- Quoted from object classes, added and unchanged since revision 8, 22 Jan 2018.

While the initial definition of Object Class would have required the SCP to pose a danger, the current doesn't. However, as @Jacob Masters stated, both criteria are met.
Although in my opinion a sentient being/beings with the ability to throw a moon around should be considered dangers, even without predicated impact with Earth.

item.content:encoded:
This post went from 'huh, that's a neat little quirk', to interesting, to 'oh crap' very nicely. The image of someone/thing running iterative tests to slam Iapetus into Earth was -not- what I was expecting until near the end of the article.

The 'Going to kill you all' message at the end was phrased just non-obviously enough not to trigger an immediate eyerolling. I can only presume the moon's controller believes it's going to take 17 iterations to achieve maximun human extinction without over a century of waiting first.

Which to me, is begging the question: It's obvious that Iapetus turning kamikaze was triggered by Earth sending a flyby through Saturn's system. So what is going on over there that the natives don't want Earth to know about? Or is our probe just viewed as the precursor of an invasion and they're trying to get the first blow in?

Final bit of triggered speculation: What if it's the Saturn system itself doing this? The equivalent of throwing a shoe at someone who's bothering you?

Regardless, I enjoy this. As you can tell, it sparked my imagination in a big way. I like it.

item.title: I can't help but wonder about the intelligence bit
item.content:encoded:
Considering the repeated deviations, the increasing chance of colliding with Earth, decreasing time to impact event, eccentricity variance, I would be inclined to believe that this is not an intelligence-driven anomaly. It's clearly running a genetic algorithm, with the end parameters set at collision with Earth in the least amount of time.

The year-long gap following 5/31/09, followed by a massive increase in accuracy by 6/1/10, tells me that the first five were a single "generation", and the year was spent "breeding" the results. This is, though, all without a decent calculator handy to crunch the actual numbers. So I could be wrong.
